title: Flaky: restart mid-resolve (disk lost) adopts a cancelled implement attempt instead of continuing the resolve job
description:
TestARestartMidResolveWaitsForTheResolveJobInsteadOfJudgingItsStartingCommit (internal/reconcile/resolve_resume_test.go) failed once in CI, in the subtest "the worker and its state are gone". It passed on a re-run of the same commit. Flaky means bug: find the race and fix it.

Where it failed: PR #135, head cb4d3c49, CI run 36559158827 attempt 1, job 109375550361 (`go`, 2026-09-29T11:12Z). The `go` job passed on attempt 2 at the same commit.

Full failure output:

    --- FAIL: TestARestartMidResolveWaitsForTheResolveJobInsteadOfJudgingItsStartingCommit (19.90s)
        --- FAIL: TestARestartMidResolveWaitsForTheResolveJobInsteadOfJudgingItsStartingCommit/the_worker_and_its_state_are_gone (10.18s)
            resolve_resume_test.go:175: a2 was rejected on resume: missing-result: the attempt was cancelled: its credential was revoked and then it was stopped
            resolve_resume_test.go:207: the resume recorded no "started again from the head it pushed" for the resolve job: [adopted waiting collected rejected_work_carried rejected cleaned_up cleaned_up settled tier_derived claimed carried dispatched waiting collected cleaned_up dispatched collected integrated cleaned_up integrated gate_started gate_passed published published closed cleaned_up cleaned_up]
    FAIL	github.com/pengelbrecht/ticfac/internal/reconcile	555.589s

What the output shows: the resumed incarnation ADOPTED a2's implement attempt, which then collected as cancelled ("credential revoked and then stopped"). The collect rejected it, and the run carried and redispatched it. The resolve job was never continued "from the head it pushed". So in the disk-lost branch, the first incarnation's Evacuate("terminated") appears to have cancelled a2's main attempt. The resume then took that attempt as live, instead of reaching the resolve job. This looks timing-dependent: which job the evacuation found in flight, and whether the main attempt had settled before the SIGTERM flush.

Related, possibly the same root cause: main's CI at 7fce53c5 (run 36557718336) failed TestAResolveJobThatEndsItsTurnEarlyIsNudgedAndTheRunCompletes, another resolve-path test.

Not caused by #135. That PR changes only foreign-claim handling: the holder is asked only when Options.ClaimHolder is set, and the fixture leaves it nil. The takeover needs a stale foreign claim. A carry-chain link with an empty run_id reads this run's own store, as before. This test has one run id and no foreign markers. Also, 20 recent failed CI runs across branches show no failure of this test.

Stress harness (does not reproduce locally yet): 50/50 passes with -race at both base 9fd73ef9 and cb4d3c49, run concurrently at nice 15 on the shared Mac:

    go test -c -race -o /tmp/reconcile.test ./internal/reconcile/
    cd internal/reconcile && nice -n 15 /tmp/reconcile.test \
      -test.run 'TestARestartMidResolveWaitsForTheResolveJobInsteadOfJudgingItsStartingCommit' \
      -test.count=50 -test.parallel 4 -test.timeout 90m

The CI runner is slower. To widen the window, try the harness under CPU load (for example, run the full ./internal/reconcile suite beside it, or GOMAXPROCS=1). The target is a deterministic reproduction: inject a delay between Evacuate's snapshot and the kill, or between the main attempt's settle and the flush.
closed_reason: Fixed: (1) a subprocess Cancel of an attempt that has reported now gives it a bounded grace to settle on its own before writing a cancellation, so releaseWorker no longer renames a collected-succeeded attempt 'cancelled' for a resume; (2) the supervisor announces a nudge before starting the nudged runner, and Inspect (subprocess and herdr) decides state before reading the observation stream. Deterministic repros in executor_test.go, nudge_order_test.go and resolve_resume_test.go (CONFLICT_LINGER).
